node: Dispatchable power equipment, gas turbines, balance-of-plant, and backup generation
summary: Layer 1B expands the dispatchable-power and balance-of-plant universe using a two-lane funnel. GE Vernova is retained only as a high-attention reference anchor because its gas-turbine backlog and data-center electrification orders validate demand. The underfollowed lane focuses on smaller public suppliers with direct or adjacent exposure: Power Solutions International for standby/prime/microgrid power systems used in data-center markets, CECO Environmental for power-generation emissions/exhaust/engineered systems and a reported major datacenter-powergen order, and Graham Corporation as a weaker but relevant hypothesis through heat-transfer, fluid-management, turbomachinery, SMR and power-production equipment. Key uncertainty: evidence is strongest where company filings explicitly mention data centers or power-generation bookings; weaker candidates need customer/order-level verification before later Serenity layers.
